goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Guests are persisted to the DB before the calendar sync call, with no transaction or rollback, so a calendar-sync failure leaves attendees committed without a confirmed invite.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code first persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. There is no Prisma transaction wrapping the DB write + calendar sync, and no compensating rollback/delete if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws. Since that calendar call is not inside a try/catch, any failure will abort the handler after the DB commit, leaving guests stored in the DB without the calendar being updated/synced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:124 — The CalendarEvent passed to sendAddGuestsEmails never sets the team field, so team members are silently never notified of the added guest.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the constructed `evt: CalendarEvent` includes `organizer`, `attendees`, `destinationCalendar`, etc., but never sets a `team` property (nor does the booking query include team members data). In email-manager.ts `sendAddGuestsEmails` calls `formatCalEvent(calEvent)` and then only notifies team members inside `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { ... }`. With `evt.team` unset, `calendarEvent.team` will be undefined (absent any evidence in this diff that `formatCalEvent` can infer/populate team members from other fields), so team members will not be emailed despite the code intending to do so.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:28 — Organizer email subject uses calEvent.attendees[0].name instead of organizer/team name, and new guests are created with an empty name, risking a blank subject.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the email subject is built with `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` (line ~28 in the diff). In the new `addGuests.handler.ts`, newly-added guests are created with `name: ""` (`guestsFullDetails` sets `name: ""`). Since `calEvent.attendees` is populated from the booking attendees (including the newly created ones) and attendee ordering is not guaranteed, `attendees[0]` can be a newly-added guest with an empty name, producing a subject like `Guests Added: <eventType> with  at <date>`. Also, even when non-empty, using the first attendee’s name is inconsistent with the attendee template which uses `team?.name || organizer.name` and likely incorrect for an organizer-facing email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:169 — The catch block around sendAddGuestsEmails discards the actual error object and only logs a static string via console.log.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts, the code wraps `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` in `try/catch`, but the `catch (err)` block only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and never logs/records the actual `err`. This is directly visible in the diff and results in lost diagnostic information when email sending fails (reduced observability and harder debugging).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:46 — The "Remove email" tooltip text is hardcoded in English instead of using the component's useLocale/t() translation function.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the component imports and initializes `useLocale()` (`const { t } = useLocale();`) and uses `t(...)` for other UI strings (e.g., `t("add_another")`). However, the tooltip is rendered as `<Tooltip content="Remove email">`, which is a hardcoded English string and not passed through `t()`. This is a verifiable i18n/localization defect introduced in the diff.
